welcome_lead: From Friday-night candles to Yom Kippur fasts, explore the rhythms of Jewish life.

walkthroughs.body_html: Shabbat begins at sundown on Friday with the lighting of candles, blessings over wine (kiddush) and bread (challah). It ends at nightfall on Saturday with Havdalah. Heschel called Shabbat 'a sanctuary in time' — a weekly experience of liberation and renewal.

Kashrut distinguishes permitted (kosher) from forbidden foods. Mammals must chew the cud and have split hooves; only certain fish (with fins and scales) and birds are permitted; meat and dairy are kept separate. Ritual slaughter (shechita) by a shochet is required for meat.

The festival calendar weaves agricultural, historical and theological themes: Pesach (Exodus), Shavuot (Torah at Sinai), Sukkot (wilderness wandering), Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur (judgement and atonement), Hanukkah and Purim. Yom HaShoah honours victims of the Holocaust.

mcqs.q: What does Kant's categorical imperative require?
options: Treat others how you would like to be treated.
The covenant means Jews must not interact with non-Jews.
Do whatever your conscience tells you to do.
Acting only on maxims you could will to be universal laws, and treating people as ends in themselves, never merely as means.

mcqs.q: What does the Abrahamic covenant in Judaism involve?
options: Atonement means Jesus apologised to humans for being born divine.
Being 'chosen' means Jews believe they are superior to other peoples.
God's promise to Abraham of land, descendants and blessing, in return for faithfulness — the foundational covenant marking Jews as a covenant people with responsibilities, not privileges.
The covenant means Jews must not interact with non-Jews.
